C0.quote: voting rules that are computable by querying voters about
C0.note: Studies whether single-winner voting rules can be computed from restricted subset queries of an underlying preference profile.

C1.quote: fully characterizes the set of positional scoring rules that can be computed
C1.note: Information-theoretic computability characterisation (which rules have the property of being computable with t-queries) plus query-complexity bounds. Coded AL primary because both parts concern what algorithms can compute.

C2.1.quote: A voting rule f maps preference profiles to a set

C2.2.quote: A ranking or preference over a set C of m candidates
C2.2.note: Profiles are distributions over strict rankings; queries return restrictions to subsets.

C2.3.quote: rankings of the m candidates representing the underlying voter preferences

C2.4.quote: is a distribution σ over preferences L(C), representing the proportion
C2.4.note: The rule and the queries are applied directly to the preference distribution. No statement is made about truthful reporting.

C3.2.loc: Introduction; Section 2 (Preliminaries, incl. 2.3 Query model); Section 6 Discussion
C3.2.note: Query responses are defined as restrictions of the held rankings, but there is no sentence saying voters answer sincerely.

C4.1.note: Distortion is mentioned only as related work. The paper itself uses no utility, welfare or distortion notion for voters.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.note: Results concern computability and query complexity, not welfare or representation.

VOT.quote_behav: a voter σ ∼ σ arrives, and the algorithm learns σ|Q
VOT.note: Voters' responses are mechanically the restriction of their ranking. The query algorithm/platform is treated as an algorithm, not as a modelled agent with an objective.

C9.2.quote: a voter σ ∼ σ arrives, and the algorithm learns σ|Q
C9.2.note: The claims concern computability, so the needed assumption is that query responses are restrictions of an underlying full ranking. This is stated in the query model. No welfare or strategic assumptions are needed.
